points: Security forces killed 15 terrorists in two separate operations in Mastung, Balochistan, under Operation Raddul Fitna 3.
The operation cleared several areas including Killi Pasand Khan, Musa Khan, Khorasani, and Kaftari of terrorist presence.
State media identified the targeted groups as Fitna al Hindustan, a designation used for the outlawed Balochistan Liberation Army.
China has renewed its call at the UN Security Council for the 1267 Committee to place the BLA and its Majeed Brigade on the international sanctions list.
Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik attended the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, the first Pakistani minister to visit India since May 2023.
Minister Malik described climate change as the primary enemy of South Asian civilisations during the forum.
Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stated that Pakistan believes in multilateralism and rejects bloc or unilateral politics.
An Indian national, Nikhil Gupta, was sentenced to 235 months in a US court for his role in a 2023 plot to assassinate a Sikh leader in the United States.
President Asif Ali Zardari promulgated five ordinances affecting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including one removing protection for MPAs against preventive detention.
New ordinances established Area Representative and Development Councils to oversee development initiatives in 12 districts of KP.
The government has invited the PTI to join the National Assembly Electoral Reforms Committee with representation proportional to its seats.
The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, is facing a deadlock as negotiators struggle to reach a consensus on fossil fuel transitions and climate finance.
The draft agreement removed explicit references to transitioning away from coal, oil, and gas and dropped a target of $120 billion for adaptation finance by 2035.
Climate experts highlighted that Pakistan’s 2022 floods submerged one-third of the country and caused widespread destruction.
Transworld Associates reported that repair operations on the SMW5 international submarine cable are expected to conclude by December 6.
Internet users may continue to experience slower speeds during peak hours as 20% of traffic remains affected by the cable fault.
The US FBI is reportedly investigating a suspected breach of the National Crime Information Centre database used by law enforcement agencies.
The Sindh Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (SICVD) provided free services to nearly 3.77 million patients between January and October 2026.
The SICVD performed 1,626 open-heart surgeries, including 220 for children, within the first 10 months of 2026.
Weekly inflation reached 10.41% year-on-year for the week ending November 19, largely driven by rising wheat flour prices.
